      <description>Casper Ruud har storspilt i Paris denne uken. Nå er han klar for semifinale etter seier over Nuno Borges.
Ruuds oppgjør mot portugiseren endte med 7-6 (7-5), 6-4. De to møttes for bare ni dager siden i Basel, og da snudde Borges kampen til seier.
Ruud og Borges kom til semifinalen proppfulle av selvtillit: Ingen har tapt ett sett på veien, og de hadde heller ikke gitt fra seg mer enn fire game i noen av settene.

Familien sier til VG at Bjørn Terje Axelsen (47) døde etter noen få ukers alvorlig sykdom.
Søsteren takker personalet på Tangerudbakken borettslag.
«Det ble en god «landing», selv om det emosjonelt sett har vært veldig krevende. Personalet på Tangerudbakken har vært en god støtte for både Bjørn Terje og oss som pårørende i den vanskelige tiden,» skriver hun.
TV-serien fra Tangerudbakken, som gikk på TVNorge fra fra 2009 til 2018, ble en stor suksess.
Axelsen står foran i midten på dette bildet.</description>

      <description>Thomas Markle ble pågrepet av føderale agenter i nærheten av Tampa i Florida fredag morgen amerikansk tid.

    <item>
      <title>NFF innfører semiautomatisert offside i Eliteserien</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nff-innforer-semiautomatisert-offside-i-eliteserien-1.18075445</link>
      <description>Det opplyser Fotballforbundet på en pressekonferanse fredag.
– Prisen har kommet ned til et nivå som gjør at muligheten er der, sier generalsekretær Karl-Petter Løken.
Han opplyser at innføringen vil skje i tråd med et dommerløft. NFF bevilger 5,5 millioner kroner i 2027 til dommerløftet, og 3,5 millioner av dem skal få til semiautomatisert offside.
NFF ønsker å øke dette til 7,5 millioner kroner i 2028, og gradvis trappe opp mot 2030.
– Det du har sett med disse linjene blir borte og du får disse visningene med menneskekropper hvor du ser helt tydelig at det er offside. Det er semiautomatisert offside. Det er det ene løftet, sier Løken og fortsetter:
– Det er en utgift som tas én gang og som vil følge oss, og så vil vi trappe opp resten av investeringen i dommerutviklingene i de andre tiltakene i tillegg. Så det blir en gradvis opptrapping, eksempelvis profesjonalisering. Vi starter stille og rolig og så blir det flere og flere.
Dette skjer etter et VAR-oppgjør blant flere toppklubber. Roenborg satt ned et eget utvalg som konkluderte med at «Dagens VAR fungerer for dårlig under norske forhold. De lovte forbedringene har ikke løst hovedutfordringene, og kostnadene er for høye i forhold til kvaliteten».
Utvalget til Rosenborg stilte seg også tvilende til at semiautomatisert offside ville hjelpe VAR i norsk fotball.
– Så det vil være penger ut av vinduet hvis tinget sier nei (til VAR)? spør NRK.
– Vi kommer ikke til å diskutere detaljer i den avtalen, svarer Klaveness.</description>
      <category>Sportsnyheter</category>
      <category>Eliteserien 2026</category>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/vg_-oslo-kutter-antall-elsparkesykler-og-hever-aldersgrensen-1.18074020</link>
      <description>– For at folk som kunne ha de samme mulighetene til å reise som før og kunne komme seg rundt uten å bruke bilen, så øker vi antallet elsykler, sier byrådsleder Eirik Lae Solberg (H) til VG.
Det totale taket for elektriske utleiekjøretøy forblir på 16.000, men antallet elsparkesykler kuttes fra 16.000 til maksimalt 12.000. De resterende 4000 plassene settes av til elsykler når byrådet nå lyser ut ny anbudskonkurranse.
Byrådet setter også en fast nedre aldersgrense på 16 år for både elsykler og elsparkesykler.
– Vi hever aldersgrensen til 16 år sånn at vi styrker tryggheten både for dem som bruker elsykler- og elsparkesykler og for fotgjengere, sier Solberg.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Boligprisene falt med 1 prosent i oktober</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/boligprisene-falt-med-1-prosent-i-oktober-1.18073195</link>
      <description>Boligprisene i Norge falt med 1 prosent i oktober.
Det kommer frem i ferske tall fra Eiendom Norge. Sesongjustert steg prisene med 0,1 prosent.
– Det er normalt at boligprisene faller om høsten og i oktober i år var prisutviklingen svak i de fleste områdene i Norge, sier administrerende direktør Henning Lauridsen i Eiendom Norge i en pressemelding.
Hittil i år har prisene steget med 3,2 prosent. I september var dette tallet 4,2 prosent.
Gjennomsnittlig tid før en bolig blir solgt er 50 dager etter oktober, ifølge Eiendom Norge.
I oktober ble det solgt 8.970 boliger i Norge, noe som er 13,4 prosent færre enn i oktober 2025.
Til tross for nedgang i oktober, har Ålesund størst vekst i år, med 10,5 prosent.</description>

      <description>The New York Times erklærer at demokraten Abdul El-Sayed vinner over republikaneren Mike Rogers i kampen om sentatssetet i Michigan.
Det betyr at Demokratene går seirende ut av en av de mest profilerte valgene i dette mellomvalget.
Michigan var den eneste delstaten der Republikanerne hadde en realistisk mulighet til å ta et sete fra Demokratene i Senatet.
El-Sayed, som tilhører venstresiden i Det demokratiske partiet, blir den første senatoren som er muslim.
Sluttspurten i Michigan har vært preget av kontroverser. Haley Stevens, som tapte nominasjonskampen mot El-Sayed i høst, erklærte søndag sin støtte til republikaneren Rogers i stedet for partifellen El-Sayed.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Tidligere NRK-journalist Audun Tjomsland er død</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/tidligere-nrk-journalist-audun-tjomsland-er-dod-1.18072575</link>
      <description>Tidligere NRK-journalist og redaktør i Sandefjords Blad, Audun Tjomsland, er død. Han ble 83 år gammel.
Det skriver Sandefjords Blad tirsdag.
Tjomsland var først å se på Dagsrevyen på NRK i 1968. I tillegg var han utenrikskorrespondent i både London og New York fra 1975 til 1983.
Fra 1966 til 1968 studerte Tjomsland internasjonal politikk ved Macalester College i Minnesota i USA.
I 1985 ble han redaktør i Sandefjords Blad, men sa opp jobben i 1987 for å bli informasjonsdirektør i Braathens SAFE/Braathens hvor han jobbet i 13 år. Fra 2001 til 2005 var Tjomsland informasjonsdirektør i Norges Statsbaner NSB.
Tjomsland ble pensjonist i 2005 og jobbet etter det som frilansforfatter i Sandefjord.
– Man får holde på så lenge det går, sa han i et portrettintervju med Drammens Tidende i 1998.</description>

CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ Independent and employee owned - local news stories, weather, sports, events and more Sat, 07 Nov 2026 03:31:38 +0000 en-CA hourly 1 https://cheknews.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/cropped-CHEK-Mark-512x512-1-200x200.png?crop=1 CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ 32 32 70014466 CFB Esquimalt welcomes new vessel following historic Arctic expedition https://cheknews.ca/cfb-esquimalt-welcomes-new-vessel-following-historic-arctic-expedition-1359804/ Sat, 07 Nov 2026 03:29:40 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1359804

CFB Esquimalt welcomed home a new ice-breaking vessel Friday after its historic journey through Canada's Arctic.

The post CFB Esquimalt welcomes new vessel following historic Arctic expedition appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

CFB Esquimalt welcomed home a new ice-breaking vessel Friday after its historic journey through Canada’s Arctic.

HMCS Robert Hampton Gray was welcomed to the Esquimalt base with a ceremonial sail past, music and family eagerly awaiting the crew’s return.

“My eldest son has been in Halifax for the last year and a half so, it’s his first time home, so it’s nice,” Chris Rorvik said.

The vessel and crew spent the last 83 days bringing HMCS Robert Hampton Gray from where it was built in Halifax to its new home base in Esquimalt, travelling through the Arctic.

This is the first voyage of it’s kind to relocate a ship from the Atlantic to the Pacific.

“It is only the third time that a Canadian warship has gone through the Northwest Passage,” Cdr Brian Henwood, Commanding Officer of HMCS Robert Hampton Gray, said.

Henwood says the Arctic Passageway is not the typical route because it is challenging when it comes to the environment, navigation and charting.

He adds these new icebreaking vessels manoeuvre well through these challenging conditions.

“This is a new capability for the Royal Canadian Navy,” he said.

“The Arctic patrol ships are capable of operating in that environment with the ice and with the weather that’s up there.”

The expedition came with several operations. Henwood says the first half of the voyage focused on demonstrating Canada’s ability to work in the Arctic.

This included exercises with several allies, including the Canadian Coast Guard, which recently integrated with the Department of National Defense (DND).

Exercises with the Canadian Coast Guard on this mission included a helicopter embarked on a ship of this class for the first time.

“This is showing the cooperation government is looking for and this is a great example of it,” Henwood said.

He says having a helicopter on the ship proved to be helpful as it was used to get people to shore, take parts ashore and move people around in a medivac.

“We also used it for ice reconnaissance, so we would send the helicopter out and look at what the ice is looking like to pick the best path, he said.

“Surveillance as well, if there are any ships up there that we are interested in keeping an eye on. So there are many different tasks the helicopter can perform.”

The second half of the trip focused on presence and security patrol in Canada’s Arctic.

Henwood says this is currently a critical focus for DND.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

“Our Arctic waters belong to us; we need to exercise the sovereignty that the government of Canada owns over those waters, and the way you do that is by having presence, and these ships are the way we do presence,” he said.

Henwood believes the voyage was a success and trips through the Arctic will become more frequent in the coming years.

Now that HMCS Robert Hampton Gray is in Esquimalt, the Pacific crew will take over.

The ship is now being prepared for a commissioning ceremony on Nov. 16.

It is expected to travel back to the Arctic next summer.

]]> 1359804 Times Colonist set to return to local ownership after 75 years https://cheknews.ca/times-colonist-set-to-return-to-local-ownership-after-75-years-1359828/ Sat, 07 Nov 2026 03:21:52 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1359828

The Times Colonist is poised for a new chapter, one that could bring the newspaper back into local hands after 75 years of ownership based outside the region.

The post Times Colonist set to return to local ownership after 75 years appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The Times Colonist is poised for a new chapter, one that could bring the newspaper back into local hands after 75 years of ownership based outside the region.

Ed Kennedy, the newspaper’s director of advertising and the author of the article announcing the potential sale, says a group of local investors is working toward a deal. While no agreement has been finalized, he says the process is nearing completion.

“There was an opportunity to bring the TC home and we wanted to take it,” Kennedy says.

The identities of the investors and the financial details of the proposed transaction are expected to be revealed when an official announcement is made.

The newspaper was purchased in 2011 by Vancouver-based Glacier Media. Kennedy says the Times Colonist continues to have a strong online presence and maintains a notable connection with its audience.

“It’s still the highest-read media per capita in Canada,” he says.

The prospect of local ownership has drawn attention to the role community connections can play in the long-term success of established businesses.

CHEK News is one local example. In 2009, the station moved to a locally owned, employee-owned model after facing the possibility of closure.

Other Vancouver Island businesses have also embraced local ownership, including Phillips Brewing, Harmac Pacific and Munro’s Books.

Munro’s Books became employee-owned in 2014. Managing partner Jessica Walker says the model helps strengthen the relationship between a business and its customers.

“I think it makes people feel that connection,” Walker says. “So many of our customers are regulars. We know them by name.”

For the Times Colonist, local ownership could also mean a renewed emphasis on reporting from across the region.

Kennedy says the intention is to expand coverage throughout Greater Victoria and Vancouver Island, and that includes hiring more journalists.

Diane Dakers, a University of Victoria professional writing and journalism program instructor and former Times Colonist reporter, says independent local ownership is particularly important at a time when communities are looking for journalism that reflects their own experiences.

“Independent local ownership, I think, is crucial right now,” Dakers says.

She believes that commitment starts with reporters being physically present in the communities they cover.

“We want news from Vancouver Island, not somewhere back east telling us what we think we want,” she says.

Kennedy says no date has been set to announce the purchase.

But change is coming.

Closer to home.

Island politicians area applauding the federal pledge to end homelessness within 10 years but are critical of the plan to reach the target.

The plan, outlined in Thursday’s federal budget, includes tens of billions of dollars over the next decade to end homelessness, through supportive housing, mental‑health and addictions facilities, and integrated social supports.

In Nanaimo Friday a First Nations agency opened housing for some of its vulnerable young adults and says this is an example that other communities and the federal government may want to follow.

The housing will give three people between 19 and 26 years old, who have aged out of care, a place to call home as they transition into adults.

“I just wanted to say that I am grateful as a youth to feel supported by my community. This gives me a chance to feel safe,” said Iona, one of the young people who will live in one of the modular units built on Snuneymuxw land.

Developed by Kw’umut Lelum, an Indigenous agency supporting nine Vancouver Island first nations, the housing includes a fourth unit will house an on-site mentor and site manager, to provide what the agency says all youth deserve.

“A roof over their head so they can focus on their education, their employment where their pathway is headed,” said William Yoachim, executive director of Kw’umut Lelum.

This is one of the steps being taken to prevent homelessness locally as the federal government pledges to eliminate homelessness nationwide.

Mark Carney announced how the plan will roll out in Winnipeg Friday and tomorrow MP Stephanie McLean will highlight federal budget investments in homelessness and housing in Victoria.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

NDP MP Gord Johns says while the pledge is a step towards what he’s been calling for the scale of non-market housing and social housing needs to be higher than what’s been announced.

“The math just doesn’t work out. They need to scale up and be building a sizeable amount of units a year to meet the demand and the need

Nanaimo-Gabriola Island MLA Sheila Malcolmson applauds the federal government taking an active role funding housing but says it should come with increased health care spending.

“Housing first is absolutely the right model. It makes it possible for people to access supports, addiction treatment but we need the federal government to fund that too,” said Malcolmson.

Nanaimo City Council is also on board with eliminating homelessness.

“If in fact that is possible I can’t wait to help be a part of that. For the City of Nanaimo it just means helping organizations like this be nimble and really supporting these community grass-roots led solutions,” said Nanaimo Coun. Hilary Eastmure.

The four-unit housing project though small took remarkably just three months from start to finish.

Kw’umut Lelum says it hopes this project will be an example for what can be done across the nation.

The Ferry and Marine Workers Union says it wants to know why the Prime Minister is ignoring British Columbia’s ferry funding crisis.

BC Ferries is the largest passenger ferry operator in North America.

Two years ago, the corporation warned that fares could need to rise by approximately 30 per cent in 2028 to cover operating and capital costs.

It says shipbuilding costs are up 40 per cent, fuel and labour costs are going up, not to mention the four new vessels estimated to cost more than one billion dollars.

The union says Ottawa covers 43 per cent of operating costs for Atlantic ferry services. But just three percent of BC Ferries’ operating costs.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

Despite lobbying by both the union, and Vancouver Island politicians, the federal budget left out any funding for BC Ferries.

Eric McNeely, president of BC Ferry & Marine Workers Union, said they sent letters to the federal government seeking more support for BC Ferries.

“Fundamentally not surprised. But disappointed. This is the largest ferry system in North America, carries more people than all the other ferries in Canada combined. And gets less funding than the rest of ferries in Canada,” McNeely said.

Gord Johns, NDP MP for Courtenay-Alberni said B.C. is the only marine province in the country that doesn’t get additional funding for ferries.

“It’s completely unfair and unacceptable. And on operating costs we get about six dollars per capita as British Columbians. And Atlantic Canada gets $125 from the federal government for operating costs. So we get nothing in terms of direct infrastructure funding on infrastructure,” Johns said from Ottawa.

Johns says B.C. deserves equal treatment for its ferry services. McNeely is calling on the new Conservative government in B.C. to demand federal funding for ferries.

CHEK News did reach out to Victoria Liberal MP Will Greaves for comment, but he was unavailable.

“Crews are responding to a transmission outage affecting the North Island. After living in Port McNeill since 1971, he says he’s seen his share of power outages.

“If you encounter a downed or low-hanging power line, stay at least 10 metres back and report it to 911 immediately. We’ll continue to provide updates as more information becomes available,” states BC Hydro.

The BCCOS says its officers continue to stay in contact with the victim’s families, the Nuxalk Nation and the greater community.

]]> 1359832 Ottawa’s relaxed foreign buyers ban will have ‘no effect’ in B.C., says expert https://cheknews.ca/ottawa-relaxed-foreign-buyers-ban-will-have-no-effect-in-b-c-says-expert-1359771/ Fri, 06 Nov 2026 23:49:38 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1359771

Foreign buyers will now be able to buy new residential properties, a model that's supposed to direct foreign investment towards adding supply.

The post Ottawa’s relaxed foreign buyers ban will have ‘no effect’ in B.C., says expert appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

A new federal budget is bringing billions for housing and a relaxation to Ottawa’s foreign buyers ban.

The foreign buyers ban is being extended for two more years, but a big shift now opens up newly built residential properties to foreign buyers, a model that’s supposed to direct foreign investment towards adding supply.

“They feel like we’re not in a good place for housing affordability. And until affordability improves they’re probably reluctant to do anything that makes it possible that additional demand will be added to a market that’s short in supply,” said UBC Centre for Urban Economics and Housing associate professor Tom Davidoff.

But both Ontario and British Columbia have hefty foreign buyers taxes.

“I think it’s going to have approximately no effect in British Columbia because foreign buyers already face a 20 per cent tax which is pretty prohibitive,” said Davidoff.

“They’ll stay a small fraction of the market. They are able to buy new homes, but I don’t think many will because of the 20 per cent tax.”

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

B.C.’s new premier-designate Lorne Doerksen says while he’s planning to scrap housing targets and multiplex rules, during the leaders debate on Oct. 14, he committed to keeping the foreign buyers tax.

“I will keep those in place,” said Doerksen, facing pressure from then NDP-leader David Eby.

Victoria Mayor Marianne Alto says what will have more of an effect in B.C. are local housing rules, and how they may change in the future.

“Will that have an impact? I don’t know i think it depends on what policies local municipalities have,” said Alto.

The foreign buyers ban first went into place in 2023, preventing non-Canadians from buying residential properties in urban areas.

A Port Alberni man is facing several drug trafficking charges following an investigation by local RCMP and the Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit of British Columbia’s Uniform Gang Enforcement Team (UGET).

Mounties say officers with the gang enforcement team were patrolling Port Alberni on June 13 when they witnessed a man allegedly commit a driving infraction.

“The man fled from police and was arrested following a foot pursuit,” said police in a release Friday.

Once he was in custody, police say they found cash, a weapon, and drugs “that were consistent with drug trafficking.”

Later that same day, the Port Alberni RCMP executed a search warrant on the suspect’s house, where they found a gun and more drugs.

Now, Mounties say suspect Corey Pouliot is facing three counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking, with one count each being for fentanyl, methamphetamine, and cocaine.

The provincial gang enforcement team says it’s grateful for the help of local RCMP.

“Strong partnerships allow the work we begin during a deployment to have a lasting impact,” said Sgt. Sarbjit K. Sangha, media relations officer for CFSEU-BC. 

“UGET officers and Port Alberni RCMP shared information and worked together to advance this investigation. That continuity is essential to disrupting drug trafficking and supporting safer communities,” she said.

The charges against Pouliot have not been proven in court.
